title: Every message that names a node says which node it is
description:
This is where the complaint actually lands. A bare id is printed, joined by commas, in roughly fifteen places, and every one of them is a sentence a human reads with no other context:

- packages/mcp/src/render.ts:80 and :83 — the board's `waiting on …` tails
- packages/mcp/src/render.ts:46 — loose decisions
- packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts:315 — what `bind` wrote
- packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts:360 — `… it no longer holds a, b, c` after an answer
- packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts:539 and :542 — briefs withdrawn, nodes flagged
- packages/mcp/src/tools/build.ts:29 — nodes heading for the same files
- packages/mcp/src/tools/distribute.ts:38, :114, :117 — assigned and passed over

Put the name beside the id in all of them, in one consistent form so a reader learns it once. Route it through whatever the data-flow decision settles rather than formatting it at each call site — fifteen hand-written formats is fifteen chances to print a different shape.

Two things the id is *not* decoration for and must survive verbatim: it is what the human types back into a tool, and it is the file name on disk. A message that prints only a name is a message nobody can act on. Update the tool tests in the same node — several assert on these exact strings.
